findings.issue: The spitter's acid projectile is a first-class entity in the design (config.ts `spitter: {... ranged: true, projectileSpeed: 14}`; CONTRACT sim.ts owns 'spitter projectiles'; effects.ts owns 'acid glob'; DESIGN_BIBLE 'Spitter — stands off and lobs acid; forces you out of cover') but it has NO wire representation whatsoever. The snapshot carries only `players / zombies / barricades / core / you` and GameEvent has no `acid_spawn` / `projectile` member. The client therefore cannot render or interpolate a single in-flight glob, and RULE 3 ('Every entity gets a visible mesh (no invisible logic)') is unsatisfiable for it. The sim.ts↔effects.ts seam does not exist, so two parallel implementers must invent one — which the freeze forbids ('If a shape is missing, STOP and report'), meaning wave 7 onward stalls the whole fan-out.
findings.fix: Add to types.ts before freeze: `export interface ProjectileSnap { id: number; kind: 'acid'; x: number; y: number; z: number; vx: number; vy: number; vz: number; }`, add `projectiles: ProjectileSnap[]` to the snapshot, and add GameEvent members `{t:'projectile_spawn'; id:number; kind:'acid'; from:Vec3; to:Vec3; flightMs:number}` and `{t:'projectile_hit'; id:number; x:number; y:number; z:number; hitPlayer:PlayerId|null}` so effects.ts can spawn/kill the glob and the splash decal without polling. Add `ACID_SPLASH_RADIUS`, `ACID_DOT_DPS`, `ACID_DOT_MS` to config.ts (the spitter's `damage: 25` currently has no stated application model — direct hit? splash? lingering pool?).

findings.issue: Draw-call arithmetic is unshippable and no budget anywhere catches it. config.ts `maxAlive(players) = Math.min(24 + players * 8, 160)` → 152 concurrent zombies at 16 players, 56 at 4 players. The model sheets mandate per-zombie prim budgets of '14–20 prims' (Shambler), '18–24' (Brute), '24–36 prims' (Abomination), each 'animate: walk / attack / dying via pivot limbs' — and kit.ts `bake()` is explicitly 'never for animated or per-frame-mutated objects'. So 152 × ~16 prims ≈ 2,400 live meshes minimum (up to ~5,000 with Abominations/Brutes), doubled again by the shadow pass that RULE 6 makes mandatory ('Real-time shadows ON, always... never disable for test speed'). That is 5k–10k draw calls/frame. kit.ts offers no InstancedMesh helper, no LOD, no per-entity merge-by-pivot-group helper, and the CONTRACT states no frame-time, draw-call, triangle or memory budget at all — so nobody's gate fails until the game is assembled and runs at single-digit fps.
findings.fix: Before freeze: (a) add to kit.ts a `bakeParts(meshes, pivotGroups)` helper that merges each animated entity down to a fixed small number of rigid parts (torso / head / L-arm / R-arm / legs = 5 draw calls per zombie, not 16–36) plus an `instanced(geo, key, count)` helper for the ~40 static rubble props; (b) restate every model-sheet 'prims' number as 'source prims, merged to ≤N draw calls'; (c) add hard budgets to the CONTRACT: ≤450 draw calls and ≤16ms frame at 152 zombies, ≤150k tris; (d) drop `maxAlive` to a value that survives that budget (e.g. `Math.min(16 + players*4, 72)`) or add a distance LOD that swaps far zombies to a 1-prim impostor; (e) make the drawCall number an asserted e2e gate, as the splat build already does.

findings.issue: The gate list is `npm run typecheck · npm run build · npm test (vitest) · node scripts/e2e-outpost.mjs · screenshot judge loop`, but the Layer-2 decomposition tables assign NO test file to any module — there is not one `*.test.ts` owner across 7 server files and 15 client files. `npm test` will therefore pass vacuously on zero outpost tests. This repo has been burned by exactly this before: vitest.config.ts carries two written-in comments about suites that 'would have silently never run' (kart client, platform). Compounding it: the e2e does run and assert (join, start, shoot, assert wave, zero console errors) — real credit — but it is single-client, so the 'Together' co-op pillar (downed/revive/spectate/scoreboard) is never exercised; it never reaches wave 2, never buys anything, and asserts no perf number. And the 'screenshot judge loop (Phase 4)' has no rubric, no per-aspect scoring, no pass threshold, and no named in-class benchmark — while STYLE_BIBLE's touchstones are 'Left 4 Dead' and 'CoD Zombies', both photoreal AAA and out of render class for a flat-shaded Lambert browser game, which is a blind A/B this build cannot win.
findings.fix: Add explicit test-file owners to the decomposition table (one per module, disjoint): `shared/src/protocol.test.ts`, `server/src/{sim,zombies,combat,economy,waves,room}.test.ts`, `client/src/render/kit.test.ts`, and register `games/outpost/{shared,server,client}/src/**/*.test.ts` in vitest.config.ts as part of the integration task. Specify the e2e as 2 browser clients, drive it to wave 3 with `settings.speed`, and assert: wave≥3, a completed buy, a revive, core hp > 0, drawCalls ≤ budget, zero console errors. Replace the judge benchmark with an in-class named title (e.g. STRICKEN's own best frame, or a flat-shaded low-poly shipped title) and write the per-aspect rubric (lighting / silhouette / world density / fx / HUD, 1–10 each, ship at ≥8) into the CONTRACT now.

findings.issue: The frozen kit cannot produce the mood the bibles mandate. kit.ts exposes exactly `mat` / `tintedMat` (both plain `new THREE.MeshLambertMaterial({ color, flatShading: true })`) and three factories `makeBox` / `makeCyl` / `makeCone`, and declares itself 'The ONE sanctioned way to get a palette material' with 'none may construct ad-hoc geometry'. Against that, the mandates are: STYLE_BIBLE 'Zombies carry a faint `zeye` emissive so the horde reads in the dark'; CONTRACT 'glowing `lanternCore`/`hudAccent` core sphere', '`lantern` glass box with `lanternCore` core', 'a small glowing `pointsGold` price sign', 'bulging translucent `acid` sac', 'downed pose = slumped + revive ring', zombies.ts '5 zombie meshes + anim states + health bars'. NONE of emissive, transparency/opacity, sphere, torus (the revive ring), or a billboard/plane (the health bars, damage numbers) is reachable through the kit — so every art implementer must either violate RULE 2/the kit's own preamble or ship the scene with no glow at all, i.e. a flat grey compound at dusk with no warm pocket. Also absent: any `castShadow`/`receiveShadow` affordance, so RULE 6's mandatory shadows default to OFF on every mesh the factories return.
findings.fix: Extend kit.ts before freezing: `emissiveMat(key: PaletteKey, colorKey?: PaletteKey, intensity?: number)`, `glassMat(key: PaletteKey, opacity: number)`, `makeSphere(r, seg, key)`, `makeTorus(r, tube, seg, key)`, `makePlane(w, h, key)` and `billboard(mesh)`, plus `shadowed<T extends THREE.Object3D>(o: T, cast = true, receive = true): T` (and make the three existing factories set cast/receive by default). Fix the two hard bugs while it is still editable: `bake()`'s docstring claims 'Returns a single Mesh when all share one material, else a Group' but the body unconditionally builds and returns `const out = new THREE.Group()`; and `bake()` calls `m.updateMatrix()` (LOCAL matrix only), so any mesh passed in with a parent transform bakes at the wrong world position — use `updateWorldMatrix(true,false)` + `matrixWorld`.

findings.issue: config.ts opens with 'Every number here is a balance *relationship* … implementers read it, never invent constants inline' — yet the four numbers that actually determine the difficulty curve are missing. There is no wave COMPOSITION (`ZOMBIE_UNLOCK_WAVE` says only when a kind first appears; nothing says how many runners vs shamblers at wave 8), no spawn CADENCE (waveBudget(10,4)=50 zombies but nothing says the drip rate, so DESIGN_BIBLE's 'Waves ~45–75s each' is unenforceable and unverifiable), no boss COUNT at wave 10/15/20, and no WAVE TIMEOUT despite types.ts documenting `phaseEndsAt` as 'intermission countdown, or wave timeout'. `{t:'wave_announce'; upcoming: readonly ZombieKind[]}` literally cannot be populated without the mix. waves.ts must therefore invent the single most load-bearing balance system in the game, in isolation, after the contract is immutable.
findings.fix: Add to config.ts before freeze: `export const WAVE_MIX: Record<ZombieKind, {weight: number; perWaveGrowth: number}>` (or an explicit `waveComposition(wave, players): Record<ZombieKind, number>` pure function), `export const SPAWN_INTERVAL_MS = 900` with `export function spawnIntervalMs(wave: number): number`, `export const BOSS_COUNT = (wave: number) => 1 + Math.floor((wave - 10) / 10)`, and `export const WAVE_TIMEOUT_MS = 180_000`. Add a `waves.test.ts` assertion that `waveComposition` sums to `waveBudget` and that the resulting wave length lands in the bible's 45–75s window at speed 1.

findings.issue: The economy is a money printer, which nullifies pillar 'The decision each minute' ('Points are scarce and single-currency… hold a breach vs repair vs upgrade'). `POINTS_PER_DMG = 0.2` and `AMMO_COST_PER_ROUND = 1` means one point of ammo buys one rifle round dealing 34 damage = 6.8 points back (pistol 4.0×, shotgun 8 pellets × 8 dmg = 12.8×, LMG 4.4×) BEFORE `killPoints`. Every weapon returns 4–13 points per point spent, so firing strictly increases the bank and nothing is ever scarce past wave 3 — repair (1 hp per point), perks and weapons all become 'buy everything' rather than a trade-off. The curve is also unlosable: `hpScale = 1 + 0.08*(wave-1)` is LINEAR while `waveBudget` hard-caps at `40 + players*6` (reached at wave ~11 solo), so pressure flattens permanently while player DPS keeps compounding (rifle 7/s × 34 × 2.5 headshot × 1.3 doubletap ≈ 770 dps vs a wave-20 Shambler's 252 hp). DESIGN_BIBLE's 'solo reaches ~wave 6–8… full 16 stack ~wave 18–20 before the economy can't keep up' and 'A run is 15–35 minutes' cannot emerge from these numbers.
findings.fix: Make ammo a real cost: raise `AMMO_COST_PER_ROUND` to a per-weapon `ammoCost` on WeaponDef (pistol 2, smg 4, shotgun 12, rifle 8, lmg 6) so the ROI on a refill is ~0.6–0.9×, and/or drop `POINTS_PER_DMG` to 0.05 and shift income onto `killPoints`. Then make the curve bite: `hpScale = Math.pow(1.11, wave-1)` (or keep linear hp and remove the `waveBudget` cap / grow `maxAlive`), and state the intended relationship as a checkable one in DESIGN_BIBLE ('squad DPS grows ≈X%/wave, wave HP·count grows ≈Y%>X') with a `waves.test.ts` that asserts the crossover lands at the stated wave for 1/4/16 players. Also missing entirely: the defeat condition. DESIGN says a run ends 'until the core falls or the whole squad is down', but no contract shape encodes squad-wipe → `ended`, and with MIN_PLAYERS=1 a solo bleed-out leaves an empty wave running with `spectateTarget: null` and `respawnAt` pointing at a wave start that will never come.

findings.issue: Every interaction the UX bible makes mandatory is invisible on the wire. UX_BIBLE requires 'downed (bleed-out radial)', 'E interact (hold for revive/repair)', and 'Action → on-screen response ≤ 50ms'. `YouSnap` carries `downedUntil` (radial OK) but has NO revive-hold progress, no 'you are being revived by X' flag, no repair-hold progress or points-drain readout, no reload state (`reloadEndsAt` / `reloading`), and no interact prompt/target. `PlayerSnap` has `downed` but no 'being revived' state, so players.ts cannot render the 'revive indicator' the table assigns it. There is likewise no `revive_started` / `revive_cancelled` / `repair_tick` event. hud.ts and ui/menus.ts are being asked to display state the contract never sends, so they will either fake it client-side (and desync from the authoritative 2.5s REVIVE_MS + quickload-scaled reloads) or ship nothing.
findings.fix: Add to YouSnap: `reloading: boolean; reloadEndsAt: number; interact: { kind: 'revive'|'repair'|'rebuild'|'buy'|'buy_ammo'|'perk'|null; targetId: number|null; progress: number; costPerSec: number } | null`. Add to PlayerSnap: `revivedBy: PlayerId | null; reviveProgress: number` (0..1) and an `ads: boolean` / `sprinting: boolean` pair so viewmodel/players render remote stance. Add GameEvent `{t:'reload_start'; ms:number}` and `{t:'interact_cancel'; reason:'out_of_range'|'no_points'|'target_gone'}`.

findings.issue: The buy surface has no location. map.ts defines four stations with per-station stock — `{ id: 0, x: -12, z: -12, weapons: ['smg','shotgun'] }` … `{ id: 3, x: 12, z: 12, weapons: ['shotgun','rifle'] }` — plus `ammoCrates` and a single `perkStation`, and CONTRACT calls it a 'wall-buy'. But C2S is `{t:'buy'; weapon}` / `{t:'buy_ammo'} / {t:'buy_perk'; perk}` with no station id, and no snapshot field tells the client which station (if any) the player is standing at. So: (a) whether proximity is even required is undefined — economy.ts may implement a global buy menu that makes the four stations, their placement, and the whole 'walk to the rack' spatial economy dead content; (b) ui/menus.ts cannot filter the menu to the nearby station's stock or show a 'press B' prompt without re-deriving proximity itself, duplicating server logic across the module boundary the contract exists to prevent; (c) the two implementers will disagree, and the mismatch surfaces only at integration as a silent `buy_result{ok:false}`.
findings.fix: Freeze the policy in the contract text ('a buy is valid only within BUY_RANGE of a station stocking that weapon') and put it on the wire: add `BUY_RANGE = 2.5` to config.ts, add `station: number | null` to the `buy`/`buy_ammo`/`buy_perk` C2S members (server still re-validates range), and add `nearStation: { id: number; kind: 'weapon'|'ammo'|'perk'; weapons: readonly WeaponId[] } | null` to YouSnap so the HUD prompt and the menu stock come from one authoritative source. Also type the failure: `reason: string | null` on `buy_result` and `code: string` on `notice` are stringly-typed holes in an otherwise strict contract — make them `'no_points'|'not_owned'|'max_tier'|'out_of_range'|'wrong_phase'|'full_ammo'` unions so hud.ts can localize them without string-matching.

findings.issue: Three ownership defects in one area. (1) `<link rel="stylesheet" href="/src/style.css" />` — that file does not exist and NO module in the Layer-2 client table owns it, so `npm run build` (a listed gate) fails at html-asset resolution the moment integration runs; and whoever eventually writes it will fill it with ad-hoc hex, violating RULE 2. (2) The 'First-60-seconds onboarding' the UX bible makes mandatory ('A 5-line overlay, dismissible… A "look here" arrow points at the nearest buy station for the first 10s') is owned by nobody — hud.ts owns 'Crosshair, vitals, wave state, objective pips, downed arrows, scoreboard, notifications' and menus.ts owns 'Lobby, buy menu, perk menu, ammo, end screen, pause'. (3) Hit markers and damage numbers are DOUBLE-owned: the table gives `render/effects.ts` 'hit markers, damage numbers' while the FX model sheet says 'hit marker + floating damage number (HUD)' — two agents, one feature, guaranteed collision or guaranteed gap.
findings.fix: Add `client/src/style.css` to the ownership table (assign it to ui/hud.ts's owner, with the rule that all CSS colours come from a `:root` custom-property block generated from PALETTE — that also gives ui/ a sanctioned colour path, which RULE 2 currently only defines for render/ via kit.ts). Add `ui/onboarding.ts` as its own owned file. Resolve the FX overlap explicitly: effects.ts owns world-space fx only (flash/tracer/blood/acid/shake); hud.ts owns screen-space hit marker + damage numbers — and delete the '(HUD)' parenthetical from the FX sheet so the two documents agree.

findings.issue: `@outpost/shared` exports its own `RoomInfo` (`{ id, code, players, maxPlayers, phase, visibility }`) via the index barrel, shadowing the platform's frozen `RoomInfo` (`platform/shared/src/module.ts`), which additionally requires `game: string` and `label: string`. `GameRoomHandle.info(): RoomInfo` must return the PLATFORM shape, so the outpost one is (a) structurally incompatible with the interface it looks like it serves, (b) dead — no S2C member carries it and room_list is lobby-owned — and (c) a live landmine for room.ts, which imports from both packages and will typecheck-fail or, worse, satisfy the wrong shape. Related gap: the values room.ts and module.ts need to build that platform RoomInfo — the game id `'outpost'`, display name, the `label` (rift/fps use the map name; here presumably 'Holdfast'), and the dev port — exist nowhere in the frozen config; `5179` appears only in a comment in client/vite.config.ts, so the vite port and `GameModule.devPort` can silently drift apart (rift guards this with an explicit `expect(riftModule.devPort).toBe(5177)` test).
findings.fix: Delete `RoomInfo` from outpost types.ts and have room.ts import it from `@platform/shared`. Add to config.ts: `export const GAME_ID = 'outpost'; export const GAME_NAME = 'Outpost'; export const MAP_LABEL = 'Holdfast'; export const DEV_PORT = 5179;` and require module.ts + vite.config.ts + the registry line to read those, with a `module.test.ts` asserting `outpostModule.devPort === DEV_PORT` and `minPlayers/maxPlayers === MIN_PLAYERS/MAX_PLAYERS`.

findings.issue: The scoreboard has no update path. hud.ts owns 'scoreboard' and UX_BIBLE binds it to Tab; DESIGN_BIBLE pillar 2 promises 'a scoreboard that rewards revives and headshots, not just raw kills'. But `RosterEntry` (with kills/headshots/revives/downs) is sent ONLY in the `joined` payload and in `player_joined`; the snapshot carries no roster and there is no `roster_update` event. So the scoreboard renders whatever was true at join — zeros — for the entire match unless every client independently tallies broadcast events, a responsibility assigned to no module and impossible for `damage` (which appears only in the end-of-match `MatchStat`) and for anyone who joins mid-run. `RosterEntry.points` compounds it: 'private: only for the receiving player, else null' requires a per-recipient roster, which is incoherent with `player_joined` being a broadcast event carrying one `entry`.
findings.fix: Add `roster: readonly RosterEntry[]` to the snapshot (16 entries × ~7 small fields is cheap next to the zombie array, and it makes the per-recipient `points` masking well-defined since snapshots are already per-recipient), or add `{t:'roster_update'; entries: readonly RosterEntry[]}` on a 1 Hz cadence. Add `damage: number` to RosterEntry so the live board and the end screen show the same five columns. Assign the tally to room.ts explicitly in the decomposition table.

findings.issue: Two signature enemy mechanics in DESIGN_BIBLE have no contract shape. 'Brute — tears barricades and knocks players back' — `ZombieDef` has no `knockback` field, and more seriously knockback is a server-authoritative impulse applied to a player whose movement the client PREDICTS with the same shared physics (`game.ts` 'local prediction (shared physics)'); with no `vx/vy/vz` or impulse event in the snapshot, every Brute hit produces a hard rubber-band. 'Abomination — a siege engine that walks through barricades' — no `ignoresBarricades` flag exists, so zombies.ts must special-case `kind === 'abomination'` inline, which config.ts's own header forbids ('implementers read it, never invent constants inline').
findings.fix: Add `knockback: number` and `ignoresBarricades: boolean` to `ZombieDef` and fill all five rows (brute 6.0/false, abomination 0/true, others 0/false). Add `{t:'knockback'; vx:number; vy:number; vz:number}` to GameEvent (sent to the victim) and `vy: number` to PlayerSnap so prediction can replay the impulse instead of snapping. Add `KNOCKBACK_DECAY` to config.ts.

findings.issue: No non-functional budget of any kind is stated, and the one that is implicitly defined is broken. Snapshots are full-state JSON (`encodeS2C = JSON.stringify`) at `SIM_HZ = 20` containing every zombie: at 16 players `maxAlive` = 152, and a ZombieSnap serializes to ~100 bytes, so each snapshot is ~17 KB and the server pushes 17 KB × 20 Hz × 16 clients ≈ 5.4 MB/s (≈43 Mbit/s) of egress, with no delta encoding, no interest management, no float quantization and no send-rate decoupling from tick rate. Beyond bandwidth there is no frame-time target, no memory ceiling, no bundle-size budget, no viewport/DPI floor (STYLE_BIBLE caps pixel ratio at 1.5 and UX_BIBLE asks for a DPI-scaled HUD, but neither is a gate). RULE 4 does carry pool / bake / no-hot-alloc, but the RULES carry NO capability guard (WebGL2 availability, context-lost recovery, reduced-motion) and no blur/visibilitychange rule — `main.ts` owns 'resize' only, so a backgrounded tab keeps a 20 Hz interpolation loop and an unbounded snapshot buffer running.
findings.fix: Add a NON-FUNCTIONAL BUDGETS section to the CONTRACT with hard numbers and put each behind a gate: ≤16ms CPU frame and ≤450 draw calls at 152 zombies; client bundle ≤900 KB gzipped; ≤60 KB/s downstream per client at 16 players (achieved via SEND_HZ=10 decoupled from SIM_HZ=20, position quantized to 2 decimals, and zombies culled to the 60 nearest to the recipient — add `SEND_HZ` and `ZOMBIE_INTEREST_COUNT` to config.ts so it is contract, not invention). Add RULE 10 (capability guard: probe WebGL2, degrade to a legible fallback screen, handle `webglcontextlost`) and RULE 11 (pause the render/interp loop on `visibilitychange`/blur, clamp `dt`, and re-sync the snapshot buffer on resume; debounce resize).

findings.issue: The 'Balance as relationships (checkable, not vibes)' section does not match config.ts, so the numbers the implementers read and the numbers the reviewers check against disagree. (1) 'wave-1 clear (~8 zombies × ~150 pts + 100 bonus ≈ 1300 pts)' — `waveBudget(1, 1) = 8 + 1*3 + 1*3 = 14` zombies, not 8, and a Shambler pays `killPoints 60` + `100 hp × POINTS_PER_DMG 0.2` = 80 points, not 150. (2) 'The first 3 waves are a warm-up (Shamblers only)' contradicts `ZOMBIE_UNLOCK_WAVE.runner = 3`, which puts Runners IN wave 3. (3) `WAVE_CLEAR_BONUS = 100; // + wave*20 to each living player` — the `wave*20` term exists only inside a comment, so it is not data any implementer can read, yet both waves.ts and the HUD need it. (4) config.ts's `pointScale` docstring says it 'keeps economy ahead of hp' while `pointScale = 1 + 0.05*(wave-1)` grows strictly SLOWER than `hpScale = 1 + 0.08*(wave-1)`.
findings.fix: Recompute the DESIGN_BIBLE relationships from the actual functions and state each as an assertion a test can execute ('waveBudget(1,1)===14', 'wave-1 gross income ≥ SMG price 1000'); change the warm-up line to 'the first 2 waves' or move `runner` to unlock 4; promote the bonus to `export function waveClearBonus(wave: number) { return WAVE_CLEAR_BONUS + wave * 20; }`; and either fix `pointScale` to exceed `hpScale` or correct the docstring to say what it actually does.

findings.issue: The model sheets name two colours that do not exist in the frozen palette, and `PaletteKey = keyof typeof PALETTE` makes that a compile error rather than a soft miss. `makeBuyStation` — '2–3 weapon silhouettes in `steel`-ish tones'; `makeAmmoCrate` — '`hazardAmber`-like stencil (use `hudAccent`)'. There is no `steel` and no `hazardAmber` in palette.ts, so `mat('steel')` fails typecheck and the implementer is caught between RULE 1 ('Never alter shared/**… STOP and report') and RULE 2 ('ad-hoc hex is a violation') — the exact deadlock the freeze is meant to prevent. Separately, the prep violates its own RULE 2: client/index.html hardcodes `background: #0a0c10`, which is `PALETTE.ink` written as ad-hoc hex inside the contract itself.
findings.fix: Either add `steel: '#8a9199'` to palette.ts now (a weapon-metal tone is genuinely missing — `metalDark`/`metalDeep` are both very dark) or rewrite the sheet to name `metalDark`/`concreteLit`; delete the `hazardAmber` reference and just say `hudAccent`. Emit the index.html background from PALETTE.ink via the style.css custom-property block described in the style/ownership fix, and add a one-line grep gate ('no hex literal outside palette.ts') so RULE 2 is mechanically enforced rather than aspirational.

findings.issue: `OutpostSettings.speed` ('a dev/e2e sim multiplier (1..20) like rift's') is accepted by `parseOutpostSettings` and consumed by the server tick, but it is never echoed back to the client: neither `joined` nor `snapshot` carries it. The client predicts locally with the shared physics and `SIM_DT = 1/20`, so at speed 5 the prediction runs 5× slower than the authoritative sim and every frame is a reconciliation snap — which is precisely the mode the e2e harness must run in to reach wave 3 within a test timeout. This is an option accepted at the boundary and then dropped before the consumer that needs it.
findings.fix: Add `speed: number` to the `joined` payload (and to the snapshot if it can change mid-room), and state in the contract that client prediction multiplies its integration step by it. Alternatively, define `speed` as scaling only phase timers and spawn cadence — never the physics step — and say so explicitly in the types.ts docstring so server and client cannot diverge on the interpretation.

findings.issue: Two boundary responsibilities are unassigned and one non-integrator is set up for broad concrete imports. (a) `GameRoomHandle.addPlayer(id, name, resume?, sig?)` and `removePlayer(id, permanent?)` support rejoin/ghosting, and `RosterEntry.connected: boolean` implies outpost intends to ghost dropped players — but no module's row mentions resume/sig handling or the ghost-purge timeout, and no constant exists for it. (b) `stalePlayers()` is listed on room.ts ('stale reporting') but no input-timeout constant is in config.ts. (c) `client/src/game.ts` is spec'd as 'Orchestration: local prediction… event → renderer/audio/HUD dispatch', i.e. a non-integrator file that must concretely import every render/*, ui/* and audio/* module — the widest import surface in the build sits in a file with no declared interface for what those modules expose.
findings.fix: Add `GHOST_TTL_MS` and `INPUT_TIMEOUT_MS` to config.ts and give room.ts's row an explicit 'rejoin via resume then sig; purge ghosts after GHOST_TTL_MS' clause. Freeze the renderer-facing interfaces the orchestrator consumes (`interface RenderModule { build(): void; update(dt, snap): void; onEvent(ev: GameEvent): void; dispose(): void }`) in a small client-side contract file written by you before fan-out, so game.ts codes against a shape rather than against 8 sibling implementations that do not exist yet.

findings.issue: PvP leftovers and an underspecified snapshot. `{t:'hit'; victimId: PlayerId; dmg; headshot; killed}` describes shooting a PLAYER in a co-op PvE game where the parallel `zombie_hit` already exists — either friendly fire is a real (unspecified, unbalanced, un-gated) mechanic or this member is dead surface that an implementer will wire up on the assumption it must matter. Likewise `{t:'dmg_taken'; fromId: PlayerId | null; ...}` gives the damage indicator a PLAYER id and no `ZombieKind`, so the directional hit indicator cannot distinguish a Spitter's acid from a Brute's slam. And the contract never states whether the recipient's own `PlayerSnap` appears in `snapshot.players` — the reconciliation loop's most basic precondition.
findings.fix: Delete the `hit` member (or state friendly-fire rules and add an FF damage-scale constant). Change `dmg_taken` to `{ from: { kind: 'zombie'; zombieKind: ZombieKind } | { kind: 'player'; id: PlayerId } | { kind: 'world' }; dmg: number; yaw: number }`. Add one sentence to the snapshot docstring: 'players[] INCLUDES the recipient; the client reconciles against its own entry and renders the others interpolated.'

findings.issue: The world-population spec and the bake model are in tension and the numbers are unreconciled. 'World population & atmosphere' asks for '~40 rubble piles / crates / broken pallets… 8–12 dead trees or antenna stubs… lantern posts every ~6m along the inner wall' — the inner perimeter is 4 × 32m = 128m, so ~21 lanterns, each spec'd as 'warm PointLight falloff' by the `makeLantern` sheet. Twenty-one shadow-casting-capable point lights on flat Lambert with 'Real-time shadows ON, always' (RULE 6) is a lighting budget nobody stated and the renderer cannot afford; and map.ts's `props` array contains exactly 10 boxes, so the ~40 scattered props must be generated procedurally by render/terrain.ts using kit's `rng` — meaning the CLIENT invents collidable-looking geometry that the SERVER (which collides only against `OUTPOST_MAP.walls`/`props`) does not know about, so players will walk through half the visible world.
findings.fix: State the light budget: 1 directional key + 1 hemisphere + at most 6 shadowless PointLights (or emissive-only lantern glass with a single faked pool decal), and say lanterns are visual-only. Say explicitly in the CONTRACT that terrain.ts scatter is NON-COLLIDABLE decoration and that every collidable object must come from `OUTPOST_MAP`; if the ~40 props are meant to be cover, move them into map.ts as data before freezing so server and client agree bit-for-bit as map.ts's own header promises.

findings.issue: `tsconfig.base.json` sets `exactOptionalPropertyTypes: true`, and the snapshot's lobby fields are declared optional — `seated?: number; minPlayers?: number; canStart?: boolean;`. The natural implementation in room.ts (`seated: phase === 'lobby' ? n : undefined`) will not compile under that flag, so every implementer hits the same avoidable error and some will 'fix' it with a cast, which RULE 8 forbids ('no `as` casts to dodge the contract'). Minor but it will burn a retry cycle on the one file everything else waits on. Related: shared/package.json declares a dependency on `@platform/shared` that no file in shared/src imports, and shared/tsconfig.json provides no path mapping for it — so the first implementer who tries to use it gets an unresolved module.
findings.fix: Make the three fields required with sentinel semantics (`seated: number; minPlayers: number; canStart: boolean` — `canStart` false outside lobby), or document the conditional-spread idiom in the contract. Either drop the unused `@platform/shared` dependency from shared/package.json or add the `paths` entry to shared/tsconfig.json.
